classic PWM: the duty cycle sweeps continuously from 80% down to 20% and back, ~2 s per round trip by default (1 s per half-cycle); slow/fast stretch or compress it to 4 s / 1 s, so the tone hollows out and fills back in
odd harmonics decaying 1/h^2; the softest of the classic analogue waves

index.note: the peak FM index: how many sidebands the tone carries -- how bright and rich it is. As it rises the spectrum brightens steeply while the loudness stays constant (a balance stage holds the level), so only the colour moves, never the volume.

mellow.gloss: few sidebands, close to a pure sine -- soft and round

bright.gloss: a full, singing brightness with rich sidebands

harsh.gloss: hard and edgy, the sidebands crowding the top

screaming.gloss: the brightest, most aggressive FM -- sidebands to the ceiling

ring.note: how long the bright attack rings before the tone darkens. Every FM note begins bright and loses its highs as it is held -- never its loudness. Low collapses to a dark body almost at once; high stays bright deep into the note.

quick.gloss: the brightness collapses almost at once, leaving a dark body

medium.gloss: the bright attack settles into a darker sustain

long.gloss: stays bright well into the note before it darkens

detune.note: a second voice offset a fixed few Hz above the first, so the two drift against each other and the tone undulates. At 0 it stands perfectly still (the static escape); higher is a wider, more present movement. The offset is fixed in HERTZ, so it is the same at every pitch -- not a cent detune that scales with the note, and not pitch vibrato, which belongs to the synth.

pure.gloss: a single still tone, the two voices locked together

gentle.gloss: a slow gentle drift between the two voices

techniques.why: electric piano / rhodes / wurlitzer / dx piano: a struck tine or reed body with a metallic attack that fades back into it; ting = how much metal is in the strike, ring = how long it rings, reed = full body to hollow reed, strike = how hard the hammer hits

ting.note: the metallic 'ting' of the attack. this is the single feature that separates an electric piano from a plain fm tone; at 0 the instrument is only its wooden body. the ting fades back into the body as the note is held -- it loses its brightness, never its loudness.

none.gloss: no metal at all, just the woody body

soft.gloss: a faint chime on the attack

clangy.gloss: a hard bright metallic clang on every note

ring.note: how long the metallic part keeps ringing before it settles into the body. short is a quick struck-tine click, long is a sustained metallic buzz that stays through the note. both ends are taken from real electric pianos: the short end is a rhodes-like tine, the long end a wurlitzer-like reed.

short.gloss: a quick click, gone almost at once

long.gloss: a metallic buzz that stays through the note

hollowness.note: the body's character, from full to hollow. low keeps every harmonic and sounds broad and piano-like; high keeps only the odd harmonics, which is what makes a reed sound hollow and nasal. 'tine' is where a classic electric piano sits.

full.gloss: broad and full, every harmonic present

tine.gloss: the classic tine electric piano body

reed.gloss: hollow and nasal, a reed rather than a tine

strike.note: how hard the hammer hits: how bright the body starts before it softens. this shapes the tone, not the volume -- a hard strike is brighter, not louder.

soft.gloss: mellow and round from the first moment

hard.gloss: struck hard, bright and biting before it settles

techniques.why: drum head / tom / timpani / taiko: a stretched membrane resonating, whose partials are NOT a harmonic series -- that is what makes a drum a drum; pitched = indefinite tom to definite kettledrum, spot = struck in the centre or at the rim, tension = slack and dull to tight and bright, damping = ringing open or muffled to a thud

pitched.note: how definite the pitch is. an ideal stretched membrane rings at spacings that are not whole-number multiples, so it has no clear note -- that is a tom. loading the head with air in a kettle pulls those spacings towards whole numbers until a real pitch appears -- that is a timpani. this is the deepest thing about the instrument, not a tuning offset: the played pitch itself never changes here, only whether the drum sounds like it HAS one.

tom.gloss: no clear note, just a low woody thump

mixed.gloss: a note starts to emerge from the thump

timpani.gloss: a real singing pitch, a tuned kettledrum

strikepos.note: where the head is struck. dead centre wakes only the modes that breathe evenly across the whole skin, which is round and deep; nearer the rim wakes the ones that ripple around it, which is thinner, harder and more sharply coloured. a real player uses this constantly.

tension.note: how tightly the head is stretched, heard as which partials carry the sound rather than as pitch. slack leaves only the lowest ones and sounds dull and floppy; tight brings the upper ones up and sounds bright and taut.

damping.note: how freely the head is allowed to ring, as with a hand or a felt ring on the skin. open leaves narrow clear resonances that sing; muffled broadens them until the drum reads as a thud with a colour rather than a tone.

muffled.gloss: dead and thuddy, a cloth on the skin

cymbal / crash / ride / hi-hat: a struck metal plate — a dense bank of high-Q resonators, all off the harmonic grid, rung by a noise exciter; weak fundamental, energy piled into the top

techniques.why: analogue oscillator / vco / minimoog / analogue synth: wave morphs continuously triangle to saw to square to pulse; drive is the mixer pushed past unity into a soft limiter (careful: it makes a saw ROUNDER and darker, only a triangle brighter); fat = detuned unison, age = analogue instability

drive.note: counter-intuitive, and this is the real behaviour of the hardware this models: on a saw or a narrow pulse, drive makes the tone ROUNDER and DARKER (the soft limiter rounds off the sharp edge and takes highs away); on a triangle, drive ADDS harmonics and makes it BRIGHTER. Never describe drive as simply 'brighter'.

worn.gloss: gentle analogue life -- pitch, level and shape all drifting slightly

old.gloss: unstable, wandering pitch and level, worn-in gear

analog/analogue oscillator instability: micro-fluctuation in AMPLITUDE and PHASE — a slow amplitude wobble plus a ~8-cent micro-detune from two incommensurate slow LFOs, so the tuning never repeats; the softened top of a discrete VCO. Not a filter sweep and not a vibrato

motions.why: dark to bright, ONCE: the spectrum opens over the note and stays open. A one-way gesture — it never travels back. Stands on its own (a filter opening) and is also the opening half of the larger movements.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice starts its movement
                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep
kpos    = min(knote / 2.5, 1)           ; one-way ramp, holds at the top
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: bright to dark, ONCE: the spectrum closes over the note and stays closed. The mirror of open_up, and equally a gesture in its own right — not a phase of a cycle.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice starts its movement
                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep
kpos    = 1 - min(knote / 2.5, 1)       ; one-way ramp, holds at the bottom
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: one pass across the spectrum. The SPEED is not fixed — `slow`, `fast` and `snap` set it; on its own it is a single unhurried traversal.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice starts its movement
                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep
kpos    = sin(min(knote / 2.0, 1) * 3.14159)  ; one pass out and back, then rests
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: wobbling, warping — around 2.2 Hz but NOT a clean oscillation: the rate itself wavers, which is what makes it a wobble rather than a vibrato.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice starts its movement
                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep
kjit    randi  0.7, 3.1, ivoice         ; the RATE wavers -- that is the wobble
kmot    oscili 0.5, 2.2 + kjit, giSine, ivph
kpos    = kmot + 0.5
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: out and back, out and back at a leisurely ~0.25 Hz — mechanically regular, like a ball between two walls.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice starts its movement
                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep
kmot    oscili 0.5, 0.25, giSine, ivph  ; regular there-and-back
kpos    = kmot + 0.5
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone

motions.why: a slow there-and-back at about 0.16 Hz. The RATE is steady -- breathing is -- but no two passes are shaped alike: a second rate in an irrational ratio keeps each pass uneven. That unevenness is what separates it from `cycle`.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice starts its movement
                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep
kb1     oscili 0.32, 0.16, giSine, ivph ; two rates in an irrational ratio,
kb2     oscili 0.18, 0.259, giSine, ivph ; so no two passes are shaped alike
kpos    = 0.5 + kb1 + kb2
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: the timbre keeps travelling and NEVER comes back to where it was. Not a cycle and not a rate: random steps at two speeds, so no state recurs for the length of any note. It must be moving within the first seconds — a note is short.
motions.code:
ke1     randi  0.30, 0.37, ivoice       ; seeded per voice -- a chord must not move
ke2     randi  0.20, 0.83, ivoice + 7   ; in lockstep. Random steps at two rates:
kpos    = 0.5 + ke1 + ke2               ; no period at all, so no state ever recurs
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: still, steady, held — no movement is added at all; the escape hatch for a tone that must stand perfectly still.
the timbre travels round and back at a steady, clearly audible rate (~1.1 Hz). Genuinely regular — a circling movement you can count.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice starts its movement
                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep
kmot    oscili 0.5, 1.1, giSine, ivph   ; regular, returns exactly
kpos    = kmot + 0.5
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: a fast, restless flutter of the whole colour -- faster than a wobble and never even: the rate itself will not settle. Tape flutter, flutter-tonguing.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice moves on its own -- a chord
                                        ; must not move in lockstep
kfj     randi  2.6, 11.0, ivoice        ; the rate itself never settles -- that is flutter
kmot    oscili 0.5, 6.5 + kfj, giSine, ivph
kpos    = kmot + 0.5
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: a regular tremor in the PITCH, about a sixth of a semitone wide -- vibrato. Not a colour movement and not a loudness one: the tone itself wavers, evenly, the way a played note does.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice moves on its own -- a chord
                                        ; must not move in lockstep
kv      oscili 0.3, 5.5, giSine, ivph   ; a regular 5.5 Hz tremor, +-0.3 ms of delay
asig    vdelay asig, 2 + kv, 10         ; a modulated delay IS a pitch tremor

motions.why: a regular pulsation of the LOUDNESS, about 4.5 times a second. This is the one movement that touches level rather than colour, because that is what the word means -- but it PULSES and never fades: the note's own envelope still belongs to the player.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice moves on its own -- a chord
                                        ; must not move in lockstep
ktr     oscili 0.18, 4.5, giSine, ivph  ; +-1.4 dB, a steady pulse -- never a fade
asig    = asig * (1 + ktr)

motions.why: a glinting in the TOP of the spectrum: the high partials catch the light and let it go again, irregularly. Only the top moves -- the body of the tone stands still.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice moves on its own -- a chord
                                        ; must not move in lockstep
ahi     butterhp asig, 2200             ; the top of the spectrum, on its own
abri    = asig + ahi * 1.2              ; a fixed GLINTING copy of the tone ...
abri    balance abri, asig, 1           ; ... matched to the clean level ONCE
kg      randi  0.5, 9.0, ivoice         ; irregular glints, never a steady beat
kpos    = 0.5 + kg
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + abri * kpos   ; so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: the movement dies away: it stirs at the start and comes to rest, and does not start again. A gesture that decelerates into stillness.
motions.code:
ivph    = frac(ivoice * 0.6180339887)   ; each voice starts its movement
                                        ; elsewhere -- a chord must not move in lockstep
kmot    oscili 0.5, 0.5, giSine, ivph
kpos    = 0.5 + kmot * exp(-knote * 0.35)  ; the movement decays to rest and stays
adrv    = tanh(asig * 4.4)              ; a fixed BRIGHT copy of the same tone
adrv    balance adrv, asig, 1           ; matched to the clean level ONCE ...
asig    = asig * (1 - kpos) + adrv * kpos   ; ... so this can only move COLOUR

motions.why: not a movement of its own: it STRETCHES whatever movement is present — halve its rate, or double the time it takes to traverse.
not a movement of its own: it COMPRESSES whatever movement is present — multiply its rate by 1.7, or divide its traversal time by 1.7.
not a movement of its own: it sharply compresses whatever movement is present — triple its rate, or take a third of its traversal time.
